geo.note: Mid-river, just upstream of the Nicolai Bridge, toward the Winter Palace.

name: The Avrora’s anchorage in the Neva
ident: Reed (App. IV) has the cruiser “anchored in the Neva”. Her commissar’s report puts the anchorage “near the Nikolaevskii Bridge”; the pin is a guess within that.

name: Cirque Moderne
ident: Reed goes “across the river” to it; it stood on Kronverksky Prospekt on the Petrograd Side. The exact site is not verified, hence the wide radius.

name: City Duma
note: The Alexander Hall and the Nicolai Hall were inside. Seat of the Committee for Salvation from 8 Nov.

geo.at: on the Nevsky 10 m before the entrance at the foot of the Duma tower (node 11387262121), 4 m short of the south carriageway (way 576484875)

name: The Nevsky in front of the Duma’s door
reed: the Nevsky in front of the door
the whole street before the Duma building
ru: Невский проспект у входа в Городскую думу
ident: Reed’s “the Nevsky in front of the door” of the City Duma, and “the whole street before the Duma building”: the Nevsky before the Duma tower at the corner of Dumskaya Street, where the entrance (OSM node 11387262121) faces the Nevsky. The Duma’s own pin is inside the building, nearer Dumskaya Street, so its bodies are drawn there.

name: Engineers’ Castle (Nikolaevsky Engineering School)
ident: Reed’s “Injinierny Zamok”, the School of Engineers, housed in the Mikhailovsky Castle.

name: Finland Station
today: Rebuilt in 1960; one fragment of the old front survives.

name: Imperial School of Jurisprudence, Fontanka 6
note: Seat of the Executive Committee of the Peasants’ Soviets; the peasants’ procession set out from here on 29 Nov.

name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (east wing of the General Staff building)
ident: The ministry occupied the east wing of the General Staff building, on the Moika.

name: General Staff building (Petrograd Military District Staff)
ident: Reed’s “great red building of the General Staff” and “Petrograd Staff Headquarters”: the Military District staff sat in the General Staff building. Its OSM element covers only the west wing, Palace Square 10, up to the arch; the east wing beyond the arch is mapped separately.

geo.at: junction of Malaya Morskaya and Voznesensky prospekt

name: Corner of Gogol Street (Malaya Morskaya) and St Isaac’s Square
ru: Угол Малой Морской и Исаакиевской площади
ident: Malaya Morskaya was named Gogol Street from 1902. The car came “from the Admiralty, on its way to the Telephone Exchange”, so the pin is where Gogol Street leaves the north-east corner of St Isaac’s Square; which corner Bryant meant is not certain.

geo.at: junction of Pionerskaya ulitsa and Bolshoy prospekt P.S.

name: Corner of the Grebetskaya and the Bolshoy Prospekt
reed: corner of the Grebetskaya and the Bolshoy Prospekt
ident: Bolshaya Grebetskaya is now Pionerskaya Street; it meets the Bolshoy Prospekt of the Petrograd Side.

name: Hotel de France
ident: The Hotel de France stood at Bolshaya Morskaya 6, a block from the Red Arch.

name: Kazan Bridge, where the Nevsky crosses the Ekaterina Canal
ident: Reed’s “corner of the Ekaterina Canal” on the Nevsky: the Kazan Bridge, a short block west of the Duma. The canal is now the Griboyedov Canal.

geo.at: on the Nevsky's axis, between its carriageways, about 45 m east of the Kazan Bridge toward the Duma

name: The Nevsky on the Duma side of the Ekaterina Canal
ident: Where the Duma's procession stood, its front at the cordon “Just at the corner of the Ekaterina Canal”: it had come down the Nevsky from the Duma, so it stood on the Duma side of the canal. The spot is ours; Reed says only that its front argued with the cordon.

geo.at: the middle of Nevsky Prospekt between its two carriageways (ways 143519865 and 143525636), on the axis of the cathedral’s colonnade

name: The Nevsky in front of the Kazan Cathedral
reed: In front of the Kazan Cathedral
ident: Reed’s field-gun lay “in front of the Kazan Cathedral … in the middle of the street”: the Nevsky before the cathedral’s colonnade, between its carriageways. The cathedral’s own pin is inside it, about 150 m back from the street.

geo.at: on the Nevsky in front of the Kazan Cathedral’s colonnade

name: A moving picture show near the Kazan Cathedral
reed: moving picture show near the Kazan Cathedral
ident: Reed names no cinema, only “a moving picture show near the Kazan Cathedral”, which he reaches up the Nevsky from the Morskaya. Which building it was is not known: the pin stands for “near”, on the Nevsky in front of the cathedral’s colonnade.

name: Barracks of the 6th Reserve Engineers, Kirochnaya
ident: Reed lunches “in a courtyard on the Kirotchnaya” with the 6th Reserve Engineers’ Battalion; perhaps the Guards Sapper barracks. Not identified.

geo.at: junction of Liteiny and Nevsky prospekts (node 1570574377)

name: Corner of the Liteiny and the Nevsky
ident: Reed’s “corner of the Liteiny” names no cross street. He comes “Up” to it straight from the Duma door on the Nevsky, on his way to Smolny: read as the corner where the Liteiny leaves the Nevsky, about 1 km up the Nevsky from the Duma.

name: Mariinsky Palace
note: Seat of the Council of the Russian Republic (the Pre-Parliament) until it was dispersed on 7 Nov.

name: Mikhailovskaya Street
ident: “The Mikhailovsky” opposite the Duma: Mikhailovskaya Street, running north from the Nevsky.

name: Mikhailovsky Riding School
ident: The Mikhailovsky Manege, Manezhnaya Square, where the armoured-car troops were quartered.

name: Hotel Astoria (the “Military Hotel”)
ident: Reed’s “Military Hotel at the corner of St. Isaac’s Square”: the Astoria, used as the officers’ hotel during the war.

name: Bolshaya Morskaya Street
ident: Reed never says which Morskaya; the Telephone Exchange, the Hotel France and the Red Arch place his on the Bolshaya.

geo.at: junction of Bolshaya Morskaya and Nevsky prospekt (node 1570574425)

name: Corner of the Morskaya and the Nevsky
reed: corner of the Morskaya and the Nevsky
ident: The Bolshaya Morskaya meets Nevsky Prospekt by the Police Bridge.

geo.at: on the Bolshaya Morskaya (OSM way 148192854), between St Isaac’s Square and the Gorokhovaya

name: The Morskaya off St Isaac’s Square
ident: Reed sees the yunkers pass “up the Morskaya” just “Outside” the Marinsky Palace, before he comes to “the first cross-street”: the stretch of the Bolshaya Morskaya leaving St Isaac’s Square toward the Nevsky. Where on it they passed him is not stated.

name: Moscow Triumphal Gate
note: Dismantled in 1936 and set up again in 1958–61 from its castings.

name: Nevsky 86
ident: Reed: at Number 86 “we went through a passage into a courtyard, surrounded by tall apartment buildings”, to apartment 229. OSM addresses the plot as 84-86; the pin is in its courtyard block (литБ), behind the street front (way/60196034). Assumes the 1917 no. 86 lies within it.

geo.note: The works still exist, but which 1917 shops survive is not established, so no OSM element is attached.

geo.at: on way/1110136096, the embankment road along the palace’s Neva front

name: Palace Embankment, the Neva quay of the Winter Palace
ident: Reed leaves the palace “through a door opening onto the Neva quay”: the embankment along its north front. Which door is not said, hence the radius.

geo.at: the opening between the Winter Palace's south-west corner and the west wing of the General Staff

name: The western end of the Palace Square
ident: Reed’s cordon “stretched clear across the western end” of the Palace Square: the opening, about 140 m wide, between the Winter Palace’s south-west corner and the west wing of the General Staff, onto the Admiralteisky. The morning cordon “drawn about the Winter Palace” is put here too, as the same cordon.

name: Pavlovsk Military School
ident: The Pavlovsk school stood at Bolshaya Spasskaya (now Krasnogo Kursanta) 21 from 1887 (under that name from 1894), in the former Noble Regiment barracks, now used by the Mozhaysky Military Space Academy; not in the town of Pavlovsk. OSM has no no. 21: the pin is in the academy’s large building fronting the street between nos. 18 and 23 (addressed Pionerskaya 28), taken to be it.

name: Main Post Office
ident: The Main Post Office (Glavpochtamt) on Pochtamtskaya; Reed gives no address.

name: The General Staff arch
ident: Reed’s “Red Arch” is the arch of the General Staff building, then painted red, between Palace Square and the Morskaya.

name: Reed’s lodging
reed: the Russian household where I lived
ident: Reed never gives the address. Walks that start or end “at home” start or end here, with no pin.

ref.q: Smolny Institute, headquarters of the Tsay-ee-kah and of the Petrograd Soviet

name: Smolny Institute
note: Seat of the Petrograd Soviet, the Tsay-ee-kah, the Military Revolutionary Committee, and from 8 Nov the Council of People’s Commissars.

geo.at: node 1597034957, where the Smolny alley (way 146426952) from the door meets the square at the end of the Suvorovsky

name: The outer gates of Smolny
ident: Reed’s “outer gate” is at the far end of “the long wooden sidewalk” up to the door; a car leaving by it went “down the Suvorovsky Prospect”, and Uncle Tom’s Cabin stood “across the street from the gates of Smolny”. The pin is where the way from the door meets the square at the end of the Suvorovsky; the 1917 gate’s exact place is not known.

name: The great hall of Smolny
note: The former ballroom where the Petrograd Soviet and the Second Congress met.

name: State Bank
ident: The State Bank in the former Assignation Bank, Sadovaya 21, on the Ekaterina Canal.

name: Petrograd Telegraph Agency (PTA)
ident: TASS’s history puts the PTA building on Pochtamtskaya (Post Office) Street; the house is not known, so the pin sits mid-street with a 200 m radius.

name: Central Telephone Exchange
ident: The city’s central telephone station, opened in 1905 at Bolshaya Morskaya 22.

name: “Uncle Tom’s Cabin”, a traktir
ident: Reed puts it across the street from Smolny’s gates; no address is known.

name: Vladimir Military School
addr1917: Malaya Grebetskaya 9 / Muzykantsky per. 5 / Bolshaya Grebetskaya 16
ident: The Vladimir yunker school’s barracks, built 1899–1901, stood at Malaya Grebetskaya 9 (also Muzykantsky per. 5 and Pionerskaya 16); the pin is on the site, now mapped as Pionerskaya 16.
today: Demolished in October 2007, except one small wing, for a commercial development.

name: Alexandrovskaya station
ident: The station west of Tsarskoye Selo on the Warsaw line.

name: Pulkovo and the Pulkovo heights
note: The ridge with the observatory, about 17 km south of the Winter Palace.

name: The first cross-roads on the road “toward Romanov”
ident: Reed’s truck ran some miles from Tsarskoye Selo “toward Romanov”; he was stopped at “the first cross-roads” and walked from there at dusk to the 2nd Tsarskoye Selo Rifles. Neither “Romanov” nor the cross-roads is identified.

name: Barracks of the 2nd Tsarskoye Selo Rifles
ident: Reed walks to their barracks “along the post-road”; not identified.

ref.q: the garrisons of Gatchina, Pavlovsk, Tsarskoye Selo were divided

name: The Tsarskoye Selo Soviet’s palace
reed: wing of one of the Grand Ducal palaces
ident: Reed: the Soviet sat in “a wing of one of the Grand Ducal palaces”. Not identified; pinned in the town with a wide radius.

name: Tsarskoye Selo station
today: The station building was destroyed in the Second World War; the present one is post-war.

name: The Brotherhood Grave by the Kremlin wall

ref.q: The Kremlin is in the hands of the yunkers

name: Moscow Soviet, the former Governor-General’s palace on Skobeliev Square
ident: The Moscow Soviet sat in the Governor-General’s palace on Skobeliev (now Tverskaya) Square.

name: Nikolaevsky Station, Moscow (now Leningradsky)
ident: The Moscow end of the Nicolai line.

name: Nobles’ Club (Assembly of the Nobility), now the House of the Unions, Moscow
ident: Reed’s “Dvorianskoye Sobranie--the Nobles’ Club”: the Moscow Assembly of the Nobility on Okhotny Ryad, requisitioned by the Moscow MRC on 14 November NS for the trade unions and renamed the House of the Unions.
